draft.why_angle: Victron's cited sizing article adds only '10-15% extra' for inverter losses on AC loads. Neither it nor the cited Renogy installation guide gives any inverter's no-load draw or turns it into Wh/Ah per day or panel watts. This page converts the maker-rated idle draw of four inverters (plus one owner's bench measurement) into daily battery drain and solar needed, and that changes which inverter fits a solar RV.

page.title: Solar Inverter for RV: Idle Draw Compared in Wh per Day
page.h1: Solar inverter for an RV: check idle draw before watts
page.desc: RV inverters use battery power just by being switched on. We compare the rated no-load draw of Victron and Renogy pure sine wave inverters in Wh per day, with today's prices.
page.answer: Short answer. When sizing a solar inverter for an RV, check idle draw as well as watts. The Victron MultiPlus-II 12/3000 pure sine wave inverter charger draws 3 W in Search mode (72 Wh a day). Renogy's 2000W UPS inverter is rated under 18 W, which is up to 432 Wh a day.
columns: Idle drain if left on 24 h

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Renogy 2000W UPS, left on with nothing plugged in: 18 W × 24 h = up to 432 Wh a day, or 432 ÷ 12 V = 36 Ah from a 12 V bank.
  • Renogy 1000W UPS: 12 W × 24 h = up to 288 Wh a day (24 Ah). That is 144 Wh a day less than the 2000W model.
  • Victron Phoenix 12/1200: 7 W × 24 h = 168 Wh rated. One owner measured 10.0 W at 12 V on a bench supply (a 230 V EU unit), which gives 10.0 × 24 = 240 Wh.
  • Victron MultiPlus-II 12/3000: 13 W × 24 h = 312 Wh in normal mode, but 3 W × 24 h = 72 Wh (6 Ah) in Search mode.
  • What Search mode saves against the Renogy 2000W UPS: 432 − 72 = 360 Wh a day. At 5 peak sun hours that is 360 ÷ 5 = 72 W of solar panel that only covers the inverter's idle draw.
  • Against a real budget: Victron's own RV example uses 720 Wh a day. 432 ÷ 720 = 60% of that budget spent on idle draw alone.
  • The '3000' in the MultiPlus-II name is VA: 2,400 W ÷ 3,000 VA = 80% at 25 °C, falling to 2,200 W at 40 °C. Plan a hot inverter bay around 2,200 W.
  • Battery current at full load: 2,000 W ÷ 0.92 ÷ 12 V ≈ 181 A DC for the Renogy 2000W UPS. Cable and fuse sizing follow from this figure.

Why idle draw matters more on solar

An inverter uses power whenever it is switched on, whether or not anything is plugged in. On shore power that cost doesn't matter. On a roof array it comes straight out of the day's harvest. The no-load figures above are the makers' ratings, except one: Victron Community member staldor bench-tested a 230 V EU Phoenix 12/1200 (rated 7 W) and measured 7.4 W at 10 V, 10.0 W at 12 V and 12.9 W at 14 V. In that test, idle draw rose with battery voltage, and a charged lithium bank sits well above 12 V. Treat any rated figure as a floor.

The MultiPlus-II's 3 W applies only in Search mode. Left in normal mode it draws 13 W, which is 312 Wh a day, close to the Renogy 2000W UPS. A shopper who won't use Search mode gets most of the same benefit by switching any inverter off when no AC load is running.

The Renogy REGO 12V 3000W adds what the UPS models lack for a whole-coach install: it charges 12 V GEL, AGM, SLA, flooded, calcium and lithium batteries from shore power. Renogy also says its integrated transfer relay 'with neutral ground bonding' switches between shore power and inverter. That matters when the inverter feeds the RV's outlets rather than only its own sockets. Renogy rates it at 3,000 W continuous with peak power up to 9,000 W.

Not recommended

Leaving the Renogy 2000W UPS inverter on around the clock on solar alone. At its under-18 W rating that can use up to 432 Wh a day, a third of a 12 V 100 Ah LiFePO4 battery (12.8 V × 100 Ah = 1,280 Wh), before any appliance runs. Under heavy load, Aaron Schubert of 4WDing Australia reported a 'warm, smoky electronics' smell from a Renogy 2000W UPS-type inverter after about 10 minutes at 1,200 W from an induction cooktop. His unit was a regional model he did not number, so it may differ from the US unit. Use this model for short appliance runs and switch it off afterwards.
